Address by President Frederick J. Krump

My fellow citizens of the United States of Oceanica,

Thank you for trusting me and for electing me as your President. I also acknowledge the years of service from the Federal Techno-Commonwealth Party in guiding our nation through difficult times.

Under the Conservative Republican Party, we will work to strengthen our economy and rebuild the country so Oceanica can rise stronger and greater.

As your President, I will advocate for social reforms and build a strong and capable workforce for the hardworking people of the United States of Oceanica. Our vision is for the growth and development of the country so all the people can contribute in building the future of the country.

We will modernize our military and boost technological innovations and research and development in the country. We will also improve the working conditions in all fields so the people do not experience stress in their daily lives.

The government will also develop programs for the long-term prosperity of the people in the country. We will develop a sovereign national fund and improve the benefits for the people in the country during their retirement.

Economic prosperity is the key to progress. We will enact laws that will boost productivity and propel the country forward.

We will also develop and implement social programs for the hybrid citizens and families in the country so they are well taken care of through the right and appropriate public policies.

Our democracy must be strong and resilient so that the people in the country are filled with hope and optimism for the future of the country. May God bless the United States of Oceanica and our democracy.[/i]

[quote=veladyn;60701537][spoiler=The Non-Aligned Bloc (NAB)][b]Jincheon Special Metropolitan City, Minhokae[/b]

It was the 24th of October and Jincheon was in its usual routine. People rushing to work, school buses carrying children to school, pedestrians crossing the street, subways in full swing; the usual. Today happened to be different. There was the Prime Minister, waiting to take the subway. Ko Jong-hyuk, an odd man at times, decided to take the subway simply because "he felt like it." There was something about the subway that he loved, whether it was seeing the bustling people or simply the trains in action, he felt alive when he didn't have to show up to work in the usual vehicle convoy that he didn't care much for. He approached an elderly woman and asked if he could sit next to her. After receiving permission, the Prime Minister began his usual conversation starter. "How are you doing today, ma'am?" "I'm doing alright, young man. Praise the Lord. Might I ask why you asked me how I am doing? One doesn't see many people interested about others nowadays." It was clear that the elderly woman didn't care about what role the person she was speaking to had. She probably didnt even know his job. She just cared about decent conversation. "I believe our society needs to  wake up, ma'am. We need to be more considerate of our elders and contribute to this society more." "You know, that's the first time I've heard that in many years. Where are you from, boy?" Gangwon Province, maam. Well youre a fine young man. Say, would you give me some advice on a birthday gift for my grandson? Here he is. She showed him a picture of the little boy on her phone, and she smiled and happily said Isnt he just the cutest thing? Indeed maam. What about a toolbox? My son loves those. May I see a picture of him? Yes maam, here he is. You youth know how to use technology so quickly these days! She said as he unlocked his phone and found a picture of his son. Oh, look at him. Hes beautiful! Thank you maam. Well, its been a pleasure talking to you. Wait. Can you help me up, boy? Its my stop too. Oh, forgive me maam. He helped her up, and the speaker came on. NATIONAL ASSEMBLY STATION. Have a blessed day, maam. he said.You too. she responded. People looked at him as he walked by, realizing that it was the Prime Minister, and soon enough, he began to accumulate a crowd. Hello everyone. Fine day isnt it? He said, as he walked by hurriedly. He knew it took him 4 minutes to get to the National Assembly Parliament Building, and he knew that if he walked fast enough, he would make it to his meeting right on time. It was only about 200 meters from the subway station, so he wasnt worried. His phone rang and he picked up. Hello? Sir, its me Chang-ho. The meeting starts in 3 minutes. Tell them Ill be there in 2. Yes sir, thank you. He hung up. Chang-ho was his personal assistant and he could tell he cared. He would feel bad about letting him down, so he sped up. The elevator doors opened right away when he pressed the button, and he walked in. There was 1 minute until his meeting started. The elevator dinged, and he walked out and into the conference room. Good morning Chang-ho, hello all. His cabinet pulled out their papers from their briefcases, pulled their computers out, and pulled out their pens. We have a very busy day today, so lets get going. First up, our Non-Aligned Bloc outline.

[b]The Non-Aligned Bloc[/b]

Alright everyone. Get comfortable, this is going to be a more important meeting. The Prime Minister picked up a pointer stick and smacked the whiteboard. As you all know, weve been laying out the framework for a deal that we think should be made involving us countries who refuse to get involved in the conflicts between EDU and THEP. Before we make this public and available to other countries, we should work on these topics first:
 - The sovereignty, Independence, and territorial integrity of all members states must be respected
 - Peaceful coexistence among member nations is a priority, and every nation must commit to rejecting
   alignment with any military or ideological blocs
 - Economic cooperation can be fostered in any major and legal area
 - The Non-Aligned Bloc will be kept open for any sovereign state that commits to the principles of neutrality, nonaggression, and mutual respect
 - Should a military conflict occur between nations in the NAB, they are expected to resolve it themselves quickly and efficiently, with members choosing to apply sanctions or call for an end to the conflict in a stern way
 - The annual summit of heads of state to set strategic direction will be known as the Council of Sovereigns
 -  The permanent administrative body which coordinates initiatives and communication will be known as the Equilibrium Secretariat
 - Every two years, a member state assumes leadership which can be used to host summits and represent the NAB Internationally
 - Members will not participate in foreign military alliances or host foreign military bases
 - The Non-Aligned Bloc will establish the Equilibrium Development Bank to fund infrastructure, education, and innovation
 - Fair trade agreements and technology will be promoted and shared among members
 - Joint research initiatives will be conducted in energy, agriculture, digital sovereignty, and more
 - Creation of the NAB fellowship program for students, artists, researches, and many more fields
 - Protection of linguistic and cultural diversity as the base for national identity
 - NAB will maintain diplomatic relations with nations of their choosing
 - NAB may issue joint statements on crises around the world, emphasizing neutrality
 - Regardless of what the NAB votes for as a whole, any nation has the right to emphasize its own opinion on matters
 - Amendments will require a two-thirds majority vote in the Council of Sovereigns
 - Members of the NAB will be able to withdraw whenever they see fit
 - The selling of natural resources between members is encouraged and viewed as economic cooperation
Is everyone in agreement? His cabinet discussed, and finally one member spoke up. Sir, we recommend that you change Economic cooperation can be fostered in any major and legal area to  Economic cooperation can be fostered in any major and legal area with permission from the authorities of that area. Alright, I find that reasonable. All in agreement say aye. AYE they responded. All opposed? No answer. Alright, Ill take it up with the King. That was rather productive, and, thank you all for your cooperation. The Prime Minister bowed, turned around, briefcase in hand, and walked out the door.

[b]Meeting with His Majesty, the King[/b]

Using the back entrance of the Parliament Building, he got in his vehicle and gave permission for the driver to start the drive. To get to Deoksugung Palace where the King lived, it took about 40 minutes. So he sat back, pulled out his computer, and started to respond to lengthy emails, requests, view national security briefings, etc. The normal jobs of a Prime Minister. The monarchs of Minhokae had a tradition of not staying in the political area of the capital, preferring to live a more private life aside from politics. Despite monarchs holding significant political power, they have all been gentlemen and only used their power efficiently. It cannot be said that monarchs did not intervene politically, though. Whenever the rare times came up when parliamentarians would become uncivil and sometimes even have physical altercation, the King would pay a surprise visit to the National Assembly and harshly rebuke them. He wouldnt leave until they apologized to one another, and sorted out their problems. They would feel ashamed, while the King would enjoy himself. He offered advice to his ministers very often, and would keep them in check. Of course, he couldnt propose laws, but could veto them and act in his own right only in times of national emergency. The population itself enjoyed many laughs seeing parliamentarians being rebuked by the King, and it was a primary component of the Kings popularity. He kept up with the times, and made regular visits all around Minhokae, including rural, urban, and suburban areas alike, though he liked rural areas the most. Many times he would crack a joke or two, and but is also very smart. Educated at the University of Jincheon with a major in political science and a minor in geography, its safe to say that politicians did not outmaneuver him. Though he granted substantial rights to Parliament, his ministers, and the Prime Minister himself, he held the ultimate political authority in the country, which is largely based on tradition and respect for the monarch. Minhoake is a very traditional country. King Peter Chung Soon-taick (baptismal name Peter), of the Chung Dynasty did not care for politics much, but acted in the interest of his country. He was a patriot, there was no denying that. Whenever a political stance of Minhokae was to be advocated abroad, he sent ambassadors, but when there wasnt, he would go himself. The King never got into any political debates, but it was clear where he stood in many many aspects. As such, politicians generally avoided those questions around him, unless the King felt that they were trying to seek his approval in something controversial that he would not take part in. Knowing this, the Prime Minister held high respect for the King, and had careful and calculated conversations with him. Right here please, thank you. He got out of the car and began to walk up the stairs towards the Kings Audience Room, where the monarch had weekly consultations with the Prime Minister. Inside, the King fixed his watch on his wrist, adjusted his shirt collar, fixed the cuffs on his wrists, and stood up straight.  A man walked in and bowed. The Prime Minister is has arrived, sir the man was Do-yun Park, his aide-de-camp and personal secretary. Thank you, Do-yun. Send him in. Do-yun bowed and opened the doors. The Prime Minister walked in, bowed, and said Your Majesty, it brings me the greatest pleasure to speak with you again today. Prime Minister, great to see you again. Please, sit down. The two sat down, and the King started the conversation. Tell me, whats new? Political updates and personal ones as well. Ill save the best for last so why not start on the political updates? Certainly, sir. We have some news regarding the Non-Aligned Bloc proposal that we spoke about earlier. Do tell. Well, we have the framework for the proposal. Perhaps Your Majesty would like to see them? Certainly. The King read them over. Tricky times were in, arent we? All anyone wants nowadays is war, war, war. When will it ever end? I dont know sir. But we put all our trust in God. Amen, that I will always trust. With Your Majestys permission, I would like to propose this on the international stage. The THEP and EDU alliances have been far too aggressive and threatened peace, which we believe in, and this alliance can finally be a firm response from the rest of us saying: No. We dont want to be involved. I think all war is horrible and must be stopped. If we can say that we want peace, then thats what well do. The King responded in a neutral way as best he could, but it was obvious that the King stood in solidarity for peace. Thank you very much sir. Now, about your son. Sorry, your 2 sons. How are they holding up? I understand the oldest is 12 now? Yes sir, Sang-won has an interest in geography. My daughter Hue-jin is 9 years old and likes to research agriculture and my youngest, Soo-han loves anything that requires fixing. Her always has his toolbox with him. Wonderful, wonderful. And your wife, I hear you two are excpecting another child soon. Yes sir. It keeps me up at night. But I know that everything rests in Gods hands. Amen, may God help you. Likewise, Your Majesty. Prime Minister, its been an honor. They both stood up. Indeed it has, Your Majesty. I look forward to our next meeting. As do I. Safe travels. The Prime Minister bowed and left the room, feeling happy not just at the Kings endorsement of the bloc proposal, but at the personal conversation that they had about his family. He got in his car, knowing that his next destination was Parliament. National Assembly Parliament Building, please. Certainly, sir. The 40 minute drive back to the center of Jincheon gave the Prime Minister time to formulate his opening to introduce the bill to parliament.

[b]The Prime Ministers Speech to Parliament[/b]

42 minutes later, the Prime Minister arrived through the front entrance of the parliament building. He thanked the driver, closed his door, and walked up the steps, briefcase in hand. It was the expectation of the monarch for the Prime Minister to not announce whether they have approved or disapproved of their agenda to preserve neutrality, but if a situation arose that the monarch did not approve of the Prime Ministers agenda that he would propose to parliament, he would not bring it up to parliament or hold off on it until he had negotiated the agenda with the monarchs approval. In this way, the voting and debating stages were sped up, oftentimes due to the monarchs vouching for bi-partisan support. As soon as he walked in, he was swarmed by reporters and simply said Youll get my opinions on whatever you have to ask me after we have our parliamentary session. He checked his watch. 2 minutes left. He took his place in the parliament building, nodding politely to those around him in accordance with tradition. A minute passed, and the Speaker of the National Assembly walked in, leading to everyone standing up in respect. Speaker Kyung Sang Lee walked up to the podium. Honorable members of the National Assembly, he began. Good afternoon. I nearby declare the opening of todays plenary session of the 22nd National Assembly. Remember that when we gather in this chamber, we respect our cultural values, common expectation, and the people who have elected us into into our positions. Todays agenda includes the Prime Ministers Non-Aligned Bloc proposal, a proposal meant to create a bloc of nations who refuse to take sides with the THEP and EDU military alliances. Please remember to show respect, and as always, be reasonable. Clerk, please call the role. Clerk Cheong Jin-suk called the names of the parliamentarians, and with that the Speaker rose up and spoke. The Right Honorable Prime Minister will now address the Assembly. The Prime Minister walked up to the podium. Thank you, Mr. Speaker. Presented in front of all you is the proposal to create an international bloc of non-aligned nations who refuse to take part in the wars between the THEP and EDU alliances. I know youve had time to read it, but here are some key points that I want to emphasize. First, the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of all members states must be respected. I would find it really treasonous if the opposition wouldnt support the proposal, including this article. He said while smirking at the opposition. Second, peaceful coexistence among member nations is a priority, and every nation must commit to rejecting alignment with any military or ideological blocs. And third, members will not participate in foreign military alliances or host foreign military bases. I yield my time to the Leader of the Opposition. Choi Kwang-hee, the Leader of the Opposition, stood up. Mr. Speaker, contrary to what the Prime Minister is saying about us, we actually are not particularly against the idea. You know, when you compare him and his rats for Ministers-" Im going to ask the Right Honorable Leader of the Opposition to withdraw that comment or exchange it for a more parliamentary word. Mr. Speaker, I change my word to ill-guided and will continue my sentence with him and his ill-guided ministers. The Speaker looked at him sternly and sat down. The opposition laughed at the ruling party and in return the ruling party responded with insults of their own. The Speaker once again had to stand up, and he banged the gavel. ORDER, ORDER. Calm yourselves. The Right Honorable Leader of the Opposition may continue. announced the Speaker. Thank you, Mr. Speaker. As I was saying, I would like if the Prime Minister and his ill-guided Ministers would elaborate exactly on what peaceful coexistence means. They have a tendency to word things very vaguely to get their agendas across. He sat down. Mr. Speaker, what the Leader of the Opposition doesnt know is that its really self-explanatory. The ruling party erupted in laughter, and the Speaker once again stood up ORDER, ORDER. Do I have to remind you all again to be quiet? This is basic social etiquette. The Right Honorable Prime Minister may continue. If the Leader of the Opposition opposition really wants an explanation, it literally means that all nations of this proposed bloc will pledge to cooperate in terms of energy, agriculture, digital sovereignty, research, art, cultural diversity, and much more. Its right there, just not in separate lines. Mr. Speaker, what the Prime Minister doesnt understand is that his bloated language really needs to be clearly defined in the same sentence.  But, now that weve gotten his definition, lets vote on it, shall we? The Speaker stood up. Does the Right Honorable Prime Minister approve of this request? Yes, I do Mr. Speaker, a general vote may be called. Members of the Assembly, the debate on the proposal of the Non-Aligned Bloc has concluded. I now call a division of the assembly. Please line up in an orderly fashion and go to the designated voting stations for the votes to be cast. The parliamentarians voted, and the Speaker stood up to announce the results. The proposal has passed with 263 votes in favor and 37 votes against. If there is no further business, the meeting will be dismissed, and no further debate or voting will take place. Is there anyone who objects to this? No one objected. If not, this meeting is dismissed. He banged the gavel, and the parliamentarians left the assembly in an orderly fashion.

[b]The Kings Royal Assent Granted[/b]

The King, hearing that the motion had passed parliament, didnt waste any time to go to to the National Assembly Building. He practiced his input which he would state regarding the passing of the motion, waved to people along the way, and engaged in normal conversation with his driver. Once he got there, he was greeted by the Prime Minister and the Leader of The Opposition. They both bowed, walked with him to the signing table, and the King sat down and signed it into law. The spectators, the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition clapped. To booster bi-partisan cooperation in the National Assembly, the King facilitated a handshake between the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, while keeping his hands around theirs to show that it was indeed by his will that they shook hands. The King knew how to navigate politics very well. The King waited for the applause to die down, adjusted his microphone, and said a word regarding the newly-signed law. Friends, we are gathered here today to witness an effort of bi-partisan cooperation to promote world peace, the interests of Minhokae on the world stage, prosperity, and most of all, the ability for countries to Just Say No to violence. I hereby invite other countries to join this initiate in the interest of preserving peace and order, and most importantly, to promote friendship. God Bless you all and thank you for coming. May this be a new era for Minhokae and its people, and for every country that chooses to join the Non-Aligned Bloc. The King was careful not to mention THEP and EDU in his speech to prevent international condemnation, but nevertheless, it was clear where he stood. The Non-Aligned Bloc was now available for international cooperatioon.[/spoiler]

TLDR; Minhokae has created the Non-Aligned Bloc, a bloc where countries promise not to join military or ideological blocs and stay neutral in military conflict. Any countries who wish to join may join.[/quote]
